instruction.text: Here is a picture of the Earth rotating around the Sun. Find the Sun to learn more.

feedback.end: The Earth goes around the Sun once a year. At different points of the year, either the northern half or the southern half of the Earth tilts more towards the Sun. This is what causes our seasons!

instruction.text: Here is a picture of the Earth from June to August.

hint.text: The Sun is our planet’s heat source. Which half of the Earth is tilted towards the Sun?

atoms.a: Select the half of the Earth that you think is hottest at this time.

text: During this time, the northern half is tilted towards the Sun, so it is hottest there. The UK is in the northern half, so this is our summer.

instruction.text: Here is a picture of the Earth from December to February.

hint.text: The Sun is our planet’s heat source. Which half of the Earth is tilted away from the Sun?

atoms.a: Select the half of the Earth that you think is coldest at this time.

text: During this time, the northern half is tilted away from the Sun, so it is coldest there. The UK is in the northern half, so this is our winter.

instruction.text: Can you complete these sentences about the Earth?

atoms.b: The Earth rotates around the Sun ((++once 20_times)) every year.
During our summer, the northern half of the Earth is tilting ((++towards away_from)) the Sun.
During our winter, the northern half of the Earth is tilting ((towards ++away_from)) the Sun.

instruction.text: Drag the labels to the correct boxes for the seasons of the northern half of the Earth.
